reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) supports the thermal expansion matching and crack prevention of Inconel 718 as a transition layer, but only for a CoCrFeNiAl coating on H13 steel, not for repairing a nickel-based superalloy substrate. The premises about graded bonding, refined microstructure suppressing hot cracking, and applicability to superalloy substrates are not directly supported by the cited passages.
premises: Inconel 718 provides excellent thermal expansion matching and strong stress resistance as a transition layer.
Laser-clad Inconel 718 transition layers can prevent cracking under bending and tensile stresses.
The transition layer forms a graded metallurgical bond that minimizes thermal expansion mismatches.
The refined microstructure of the Inconel 718 layer reduces sites for crack initiation and inhibits low-melting intergranular films.
The intervention is effective for nickel-based superalloy substrates that suffer hot cracking during fusion welding.
